title: CorsPaint vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: HOA boards and property managers comparing CorsPaint and Precision Paint Experts: what to request on insurance, COIs, scope documents, and scheduling.
heroIntro: When an association board, a property manager, or a building owner picks a painter, the binder of documents behind the number deserves as close a look as the color chart. This is the list to ask for.

secondary: hoa painting contractors north central florida
questions: What insurance documents should an HOA request from a painter?
How should commercial painting be scheduled around business hours?

sections.h2: A bid package, not just a price
body: Your board or management office may have CorsPaint and Precision Paint Experts on the same agenda. We will not assess the other company here. When a board votes on a repaint or a manager signs a work order, they are accountable to owners, tenants, or a parent company. So every page attached to a bid ends up under a microscope, which is exactly right.
Below is the paperwork worth collecting from each bidder, followed by what our company hands over.

A thorough package protects everyone. It gives the board something concrete to compare at the meeting, it gives the manager a file to point to if an owner asks questions later, and it gives the contractor a clear scope to work from. When one bid arrives with half the documents of another, the cheaper number may simply reflect the missing pieces.

sections.h2: Documents to request from every bidder
body: A complete commercial or association bid package usually includes:
bullets: Proof of license, bonding, and general liability coverage
Confirmation of workers' compensation for the people on site
A COI with your association or company named, delivered before day one
An itemized scope listing buildings, surfaces, exclusions, and products
A written schedule, including any after-hours work

body: On our side, state licensing and bonding are current, full liability insurance is in force, and each painter we send is covered by workers' comp. Associations, managers, and commercial owners can receive a COI listing your organization ahead of move-in, so the office has it on file before a single ladder goes up. Every painter on the property is our employee, never a sub, which means the company on the insurance paperwork is the same one doing the work.

Directors get a proposal they can actually present: buildings and elevations covered or excluded, the washing and repair steps, primer and topcoat by brand, coat counts, and dates, each on its own line. Our approach to associations is described on the community and managed-property painting page, and directors will find a vetting checklist in our HOA guide to licensed painters.

sections.h2: Working around residents and operating hours
body: We plan around the hours a property is in use, with night and weekend crews whenever that keeps a storefront trading or a clubhouse lobby open. For apartment and townhome communities, a clear building-by-building sequence helps managers notify residents ahead of time. Our multi-family painting and commercial painting pages describe how we stage larger properties.

Our process starts with a crew lead touring the grounds with a tape, a camera, and a moisture meter for anything that looks damp. You normally have the written proposal one business day after that tour. Lay it next to the other bids using the document checklist above, and ask each contractor to fill in anything missing before the board votes. Nothing is added to our scope later without written approval.

For multi-building jobs, it also helps to ask how the punch list will be handled. At the end of ours, the manager or a board representative walks the site with us, every flagged item is corrected, and then the punch list is signed, leaving the association with a documented close-out.

faqs.q: Can you name our HOA on the certificate of insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. We issue a COI with your association, management company, or business listed, and it reaches you before the crew arrives.
Never. The painters on your property are our own staff, each one covered by workers' comp.

faqs.q: Can you paint after business hours?
faqs.a: Yes. Evening and weekend shifts are available so residents, tenants, and customers are not disrupted during the day.
